title: Croque Monsieur
description: Mornay-crowned, pan-crisped, broiler-finished — the proper one, with the layering that matters.

items.item: pain de mie or good white bread

items.note: quality Paris or Black Forest — up to 18 slices

steps.text: Melt 6 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk constantly 1-2 minutes without letting it color.
steps.why: This cooks off the raw flour taste while keeping the roux blond — a browned roux tastes great but loses thickening power and stains the sauce.

steps.text: Add the warm milk gradually, whisking the whole time to keep it lump-free.
steps.why: Warm milk added slowly to a hot roux disperses smoothly. Cold milk dumped in shocks the starch into clumps you can never fully whisk out.

steps.text: Cook, stirring frequently, until it coats the back of a spoon, 6-8 minutes.
steps.why: The starch needs a gentle simmer to fully burst and thicken. Coat-the-spoon (nappe) is the checkpoint — it must be thick enough to sit on top of a sandwich.

steps.text: Off the heat: stir in 1½ cups Gruyère and the Parmesan until melted. Season with nutmeg, salt, and white pepper. Set aside.
steps.why: Off the heat, the cheese melts creamy. On the heat, its proteins seize and the sauce turns oily and stringy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Butter one side of every bread slice — these are the OUTSIDES.

Build each sandwich on an unbuttered face: Dijon, a thin swipe of Mornay if you like, a generous handful of Gruyère, 2-3 folded ham slices, another handful of Gruyère. Cap with the second slice, buttered side facing out.
steps.why: Cheese on both sides of the ham glues the sandwich shut and shields the bread from the ham's moisture. Butter on the outside is what fries.

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium. In batches — never crowded — cook buttered-side down until golden, 3-4 minutes.
steps.why: Crowding drops the pan temperature and the bread steams soft instead of frying crisp.

steps.text: Flip carefully and brown the second side, 3-4 minutes, then move the sandwiches to a baking sheet.
Spread a generous layer of Mornay over the entire top of each sandwich — edge to edge, no bread showing — then shower with the remaining Gruyère.
steps.why: Most of the sauce belongs on top for the signature bubbly crust, and full coverage is not optional: any exposed bread edge burns under the broiler before the sauce ever browns.

steps.text: Broil 2-3 minutes until bubbly and golden. Do not walk away.
steps.why: Under a broiler, milk sugars and cheese go from golden to burnt in seconds.
A short rest lets the cheese set slightly so the middle doesn't pour out at the first cut.

notes.title: Mornay ahead
notes.body: The sauce holds 2 days refrigerated. Rewarm gently and loosen with a splash of milk until spreadable again.

plating: Cut on the diagonal, stack the halves slightly offset, sharp green salad or a bowl of tomato soup alongside.
elevations: Swap half the Gruyère for Comté — nuttier, deeper.
A fried egg on top: instant croque madame.
pairings: Bitter-greens salad with a sharp vinaigrette
